title: DeepSeek's Super-agent prototype: when coding agents stop waiting for your prompt

lines: What happens when a coding agent stops waiting for your next prompt?
DeepSeek has shared a research prototype that tries it, open on GitHub, under the MIT license.
Here is how it works, and what to watch out for.
Most coding agents work prompt by prompt. You ask, it answers, and then it waits.
This one keeps listening to one GitHub repository, and if you want, to a team chat app.
Someone on an allowed list writes a comment with the agent's name and a request.
Until that list has someone in it, no request is accepted.
Each accepted request becomes a ticket.
Every ticket gets its own worker session, in its own folder.
When the work is done, the agent answers in the same conversation, for example with a pull request.
It does not turn on auto-merge by default, and a web panel shows what needs a person.
But DeepSeek is clear about what this is.
A research prototype, not an official DeepSeek product, and not ready for production.
Some ideas from their article are not built yet.
And the workers run commands without asking, as the computer user who runs the agent.
A worker can read that user's home folder. So the guide says: give the agent its own account, with only its own keys.
So this is not a developer that works alone. It is a map of how agents could keep working between your prompts.
Would you let an agent pick up your issues on its own?
